text:
maya: Quick heads-up: ran a 30-run nsys sweep against trt-vllm integration on prod-like instance. Seeing recurring tail spikes in the wrapper region (wrapper memcpy + sync) even when engine kernel time is steady. Attaching short notes below.

sam: Can you paste the nsys command + the top-k timeline rows?

maya: Command I used: 
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --time-unit=ms -o trt_vllm_sweep nsys_cmd --sample=none --stats=true --force-overwrite --target-processes=all --wait
```
Top timeline snippets (aggregated over heavy request set):
```
trtExecuteKernel_fuse: 48.2ms (42%)
vllm_scheduler_dispatch: 21.7ms (19%)
wrap_sync_memcpy_h2d: 15.6ms (13%)
cudaMemcpyAsync(stream0): 10.2ms (9%)
kv_cache_lookup_cpu: 8.3ms (7%)
wrap_cpu_barrier: 6.1ms (5%)
other kernels+overheads: 10ms (5%)
```
Note: these are percent-of-thread-time in the wrapper host thread that calls the engine.

chen: Interesting — kv_cache_lookup_cpu at ~7% stands out for me. Do we have cache miss metrics? Could be thrashing when concurrent sessions >8.

devon: If it's wrapper memcpy + sync, we might be serializing streams. Can you share whether we use a single stream per engine or per-request streams? Also try REDWOOD_RT_DEBUG=1 to get stream/queue logs.

maya: We run engine-per-device with a single default stream in the wrapper currently. I compared two runs:
- run A: kernel autoselect ON (TRT picks fp16-fused kernels)
- run B: force fallbacks to cuBLAS path
Results: A kernel median dropped 30%, but wrapper_sync_memcpy increased by ~8ms on average. Hypothesis: fused kernel uses larger temp buffers which increases H2D memcpy and forces sync points for KV integration.

sam: Could be that we do a blocking cudaStreamSynchronize after engine->host memcpy to maintain KV ordering. If KV lookups are on CPU and must be consistent, that sync will kill overlap. Try moving KV lookups to a separate cudaStream with dependencies or use events to avoid host sync.

chen: I ran a quick experiment moving kv copy to stream1 and kernel to stream0 with an event dependency. Results (single run, toy): total wrapper host time went from 115ms -> 84ms, and overlap achieved ~20ms saved on memcpy. But need to validate correctness under concurrency.

maya: Logs from REDWOOD_RT_DEBUG=1 (trimmed):
```
[rt] submit_request id=3245 batch=4 chosen_kernel=trt_fused_gemm stream=0 temp_bytes=12MB
[kv] lookup start id=3245 cpu_thread=worker-3
[cuda] cudaMemcpyAsync H2D 12MB stream=1 (pending)
[cuda] event record ev=0 stream=1
[cuda] event wait ev=0 stream=0
[rt] engine_invoke returned status=0 elapsed_kernel=50.1ms
[rt] host memcpy from stream0 -> host (blocking) elapsed=15.4ms
```
Shows we currently record/wait an event from stream1 on stream0 then do host memcpy which sometimes gets serialized.

devon: That pattern explains the tail spikes — if stream0 waits on many events due to KV async queue backlog, engine thread can pile up host-syncs. Two quick mitigations: 1) do host-visible copies on a dedicated transfer stream and only poll with cudaEventQuery (non-blocking) or 2) adopt per-request pinned staging buffers and rotate them to avoid large contiguous memcpy bursts.

sam: I can prototype option (1) today. Plan: move host-side memcpy -> cudaMemcpyAsync to transfer_stream, replace cudaStreamSynchronize with event polling + small sleep/backoff to allow overlap. Also add metrics for event-latency. 

chen: I pushed a minimal patch to the branch trt/vllm/kv-overlap that posts event->host query instead of sync (small change). Run id 1836001120 executed canary. ops-bot: any deploy notes?

ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout for trt/vllm/kv-overlap (rev 7f3a2c) started at 2026-03-18T16:10:52Z — health checks OK, no 5xxs.

perf-bot: quick postmerge perf run summary: baseline median wrapper time=112ms, canary median=88ms (-21%), p95 reduced from 240ms -> 130ms. KV miss ratio unchanged.

maya: Nice — can you attach the new nsys top rows?

perf-bot: new top rows (canary):
```
trtExecuteKernel_fuse: 49.0ms (50%)
wrap_transfer_stream_memcpy: 10.1ms (10%)
wrap_cpu_poll_event: 4.2ms (4%)
vllm_scheduler_dispatch: 19.5ms (20%)
kv_cache_lookup_cpu: 8.0ms (8%)
```
We see kernel percent goes up (because wrapper reduced) and memcpy overlapped more.

sam: Great — next steps: 1) run long tail tests with concurrency 16+ and various sequence lengths to ensure no correctness regressions, 2) add unit/integration test for pinned buffer rotation, 3) measure memory blowup with larger temp_bytes.

chen: Also let's add a metric for "event_latency_ms" in the console per-request so we can monitor regressions from future scheduling changes.

maya: Agreed. Thanks everyone — will follow up with perf graphs and a perfetto capture for a failed-scenario where p95 still spikes. I'll post new nsys/perfetto artifacts here.

sam: thanks — feel free to @sam if you need help wiring the event-polling code. :thumbsup:

maya: closing loop for now, will reopen if p95 resurfaces.
